description: Developing an intelligent health monitoring system to help astronauts track their health, detect potential risks, and stay safe during space missions.
summary: We developed CHC (Cabin Health Companion), an app that helps astronauts monitor their health during deep space missions. It combines continuous data from a Bio-Monitor shirt and the cabin radiation monitor with scheduled checks such as a finger-prick blood test every 3 days, a blood draw every 2 weeks, and weekly and monthly urine tests. Crew members can also track their mood, sleep, and cognitive performance with a reaction test. The app compares every value with set thresholds, flags anything unusual as Watch or Act now, and suggests which tests to take next for a fuller picture of what might be happening. An AI summary then explains the possible causes and the steps to take, in plain language. It runs fully offline, and a built-in simulator lets the crew practise emergencies.
details:
CHC - Cabin Health Companion For Deep Space Missions condition?

Main Purpose:

The main purpose of CHC is to periodically monitor the crew's health data, summarize measurements and provide information on what certain values might mean. CHC is designed to be an autonomous onboard medical co-pilot built to protect astronauts during deep space missions where Spacecraft-Earth communication delays become significant. In case of an acute crisis, waiting for responses from Earth is highly impractical. CHC empowers crews to detect health anomalies early, prevent critical medical conditions, and manage emergencies independently.

Figure 1: The dashboard: what needs attention, and where in the body.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

How does it work?

Continuous monitoring: the Bio-Monitor shirt (heart rate and ECG, blood oxygen, blood pressure, breathing, skin temperature, activity) and radiation: real data measured by NASA's Curiosity rover on its way to Mars.

Smart status logic: every value is judged against ranges in one config file; exercise (3 METs or more) switches to exercise limits, so a workout is not an emergency.

Diagnosis engine: our code scores 22 possible conditions, sets the urgency (Calm, Watch, Act now, Emergency) and builds numbered steps. Emergency limits follow the NEWS2 warning score.

AI summary that never decides: Chrome's built-in Gemini Nano, then Ollama, then an offline assistant put the result into words. Every answer is checked against the code's findings.

Simulation and cognitive check: 12 situations to practise with one click, a psychomotor vigilance test from spaceflight sleep research, and a circle game with a crew scoreboard.

Built for the trip: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, separate data per crew member, and an optional Python server for live data.

The highlighted diagnosis engine makes the decisions; the AI only words them.

Figure 2: The crew scoreboard. For health, each astronaut is compared with their own baseline.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

What do we track and how?

31 measurements on five schedules. Each has a panel with the following sections: why it matters, how it is measured and an option to log a value by hand.

Figure 3: Bio-Monitor and radiation (Curiosity rover data).Figure 3: Click any value for its chart, limits, why it matters and how it is measured.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Case study: radiation damage to the blood

Scenario: A few days after a big solar particle event pilot Aleš Svoboda got caught outside the storm shelter. We can run the simulation using the Simulation tab.

The numbers: White blood cells 2.6 ×10⁹/L (normal 4–11), haemoglobin 12.4 g/dL (normal 13–18), daily dose 420 mGy, no fever yet.

What CHC shows: Act now, most likely cause radiation damage to the blood.

Do this now: Tell the Crew Medical Officer and mission control, protect against infection, check temperature twice a day, repeat the blood count daily, sleep in the best-shielded area. Get the Crew Medical Officer straight away at any sign of fever or infection.

Realistic: Blood counts fall only after a large dose; bone marrow damage starts around 0.5 Gy, so 0.42 Gy fits a severe solar event.

Figure 4: The AI summary during the simulation: cause, numbered steps and the next tests, each with its reason.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Benefits:

Instant Medical Autonomy Without Earth: Eliminates the danger of the Earth-Spacecraft communication delay by giving astronauts immediate, actionable guidance right on board.

Proactive Protection Against Space Hazards: Helps prevent bone loss, radiation damage, and vision issues (SANS) early through automated daily reminders and threshold alerts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Intended Impact?

CHC transforms astronaut healthcare from delayed ground-dependent support into immediate, autonomous onboard monitoring. By combining deterministic NASA-STD-3001 threshold detection with AI-generated health summaries, our system eliminates the life-threatening vulnerability of the Earth-Spacecraft communication delay, prevents critical emergencies before they escalate, and reduces crew workload during long-duration deep space missions. Beyond deep space exploration, CHC's offline-first architecture and structured triage logic can also support remote medical care in isolated environments on Earth, such as polar stations, submarines, and rural clinics.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tools, Coding Languages, Software and Hardware

CHC was developed using a lightweight, modular software architecture designed to minimize external dependencies and support offline operation.

Programming languages and technologies:

-HTML, CSS and JavaScript — user interface, interactive visualizations and health analysis.

-Python — optional local server, data processing and simulated sensor feeds.

-JSON — structured storage and transfer of physiological and radiation measurements.

-IndexedDB — local storage of astronaut profiles and measurement histories.

-Service Worker — offline application functionality.

-Ollama and Llama — optional locally hosted AI for interpreting structured health-analysis results.

Scientific data: NASA's Mars Science Laboratory Radiation Assessment Detector (MSL/RAD) dataset, supplemented by clearly identified simulated health measurements.

Figure 5: Peak at our JSON data format.

What factors did we consider?

-Communication Latency: The duration of communication between the Spacecraft and the Earth.

-NASA Medical Standards: Official human-system thresholds from NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 and NASA Human Research Program (HRP) clinical research.

-Human Factors & Crew Workload: High stress, sleep deficiency, confined space, dangerous environment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Which measurements can be performed in space?

-Continuous Real-Time Telemetry: Heart rate, ECG, blood oxygen, blood pressure, breathing rate and volume, skin temperature, physical activity (via a wearable bio-monitor T-shirt), and cabin radiation dose rates.

-Daily Logs: Sleep duration, mood, crew connection, and daily exercise minutes.

-Weekly Checks: Body mass, body temperature, cognitive reaction time, urine pH, and urine concentration.

-Every 3 Days: Finger-prick tests (fasting blood glucose, lactate, hemoglobin)

-Every 2 Weeks: Scheduled blood draws (white blood cells, sodium, ferritin).

-Monthly: 24-hour urine collection (volume, calcium, oxalate, citrate to assess kidney stone risk) and near-vision eye charts (to screen for Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome, or SANS).

Why is an exam needed?

Many spaceflight-induced health conditions develop silently over weeks or months without obvious early symptoms. Regular exams are essential to establish personal baselines, detect subtle biochemical or ocular changes before irreversible damage occurs, and verify that daily countermeasures (nutrition, hydration, and exercise) are effectively protecting the crew.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

How do spaceflight hazards affect these health indicators?

-Space Radiation: Increases cumulative ionizing radiation doses (GCR and Solar Particle Events), which elevates oxidative stress biomarkers (such as serum ferritin), damages DNA, and raises long-term cardiovascular and carcinogenic risks

-Isolation and Confinement: Disrupts circadian rhythms due to artificial lighting cycles, leading to sleep deficiency, elevated stress hormones, lower mood scores, and slower cognitive reaction times (PVT).

-Distance from Earth: Creates high communication delays and eliminates rapid medical evacuation or resupply, allowing minor untreated anomalies (like mild dehydration or infections) to escalate into critical health crises if not caught early on board.

-Gravity Fields: Microgravity triggers cephalic fluid shifts that increase intracranial and intraocular pressure (driving Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome, or SANS), lowers resting heart rate and blood volume, and accelerates bone demineralization (raising urinary calcium and NTX bone resorption markers).

-Hostile/Closed Environments: Zero UV sunlight exposure depletes Vitamin D levels, while closed-loop life support systems risk CO2 accumulation and oxygen drops, directly causing headaches, hypercapnia, hypoxia, and impaired crew alertness

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------.

When might a result warrant attention from the crew or flight surgeons on the ground?

-Immediate Crew Attention (Onboard Action): Warranted whenever a warning or critical threshold is crossed—such as sudden vital-sign anomalies, cabin air imbalances, or acute radiation spikes. Because waiting for a delayed response message from Earth is highly impractical during an acute crisis, CHC immediately guides the astronaut—and alerts crewmates if needed—to take action on board.

-Ground Flight Surgeon Attention (Earth Downlink): Warranted for gradual, multi-day trends that do not require instant emergency intervention—such as progressive bone loss, vision shifts, or cumulative radiation exposure. CHC compiles these trends into structured AI-generated health summaries so flight surgeons on Earth can review them efficiently and adjust long-term mission protocols.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

What actions can be taken to prevent a critical health?

-Environmental & Acute Actions: Opening auxiliary air vents or purging CO2 scrubbers when local CO2 rises, hydrating with 500 mL of water for mild dehydration, donning emergency 100% O2 masks during hypoxia, or moving to radiation shelters during solar particle events.

-Daily Nutritional & Behavioral Prevention: Taking 1,000 IU/day of Vitamin D to protect bone density, keeping dietary sodium under 2,300 mg/day to reduce kidney stone and SANS risks, maintaining 2.0–2.5 hours/day of countermeasure exercise, and respecting the 8-hour safety lockout after taking sleep medication.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use of AI

Inside the app: the AI summary uses Chrome's built-in Gemini Nano or a local Ollama model (llama3.2:3b) to word its text. Both run on the device. Statuses, causes and steps come from our own code.

Building it: we used Claude (Anthropic) to help write the code and documentation, and to draw the body figure, which is credited in the app. Claude also helped to simulate some of the data.
All AI content was thoroughly checked against scientific data.
